title: a label buffer counted the labels but not the separators joining them
consumer: libavfilter/vf_drawtext.c, init and the bbox text assembly
object: s->text, one av_mallocz sized as label count times label size
lifetime_ender: NONE -- the buffer is alive throughout. SPATIAL row.
shape: a buffer sized for its items but not for the delimiter between them
allocator_layer: the platform allocator itself: one direct av_malloc-family allocation, no inner layer. FFmpeg's av_malloc is malloc plus alignment.
fidelity: model consumer, real arithmetic: the sizes and the crossing expression are upstream's, quoted in PROVENANCE.md.
live_proof: absent at the pin: n9.0.1:libavfilter/vf_drawtext.c allocates `(AV_DETECTION_BBOX_LABEL_NAME_MAX_SIZE + 1) * (AV_NUM_DETECTION_BBOX_CLASSIFY + 1)`. The form without the `+ 1` is at ad956ff076ea^ and is absent from the pin.

status: built 2026-10-08; native arms measured by runners/run-native.sh in the same commit. The platform arms are declared predictions.
nested_why: the crossed buffer came straight from av_malloc / av_mallocz / av_calloc / av_malloc_array -- which on the platform is malloc -- with no AVBufferPool or AVRefStructPool between it and the request. So under this inventory's axis, WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT, this row is NOT nested.
distinguishing: the shortfall is exactly two bytes per joined label -- the `", "` separator -- so it scales with the number of classify labels rather than being a fixed off-by-one, and the fix widens the PER-LABEL size rather than adding a constant, which also covers the terminator.
